Grade: Grade 6
Subject: FRENCH

Topic 3.6: Guided Writing Grammar Handwriting Punctuation Sentence structure

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Guided Writing Grammar Handwriting Punctuation Sentence structure. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is proper sequencing of information important while writing?

1. write common words with correct orthography
2. appreciate the role of writing in interactive communication contexts

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GUIDED WRITING GRAMMAR HANDWRITING PUNCTUATION SENTENCE STRUCTURE

This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Guided Writing Grammar Handwriting Punctuation Sentence structure helps you succeed in FRENCH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Write common words with correct orthography

What this means
In this part you learn to write common words with correct orthography. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: write common words with correct orthography.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Guided Writing Grammar Handwriting Punctuation Sentence structure”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can write common words with correct orthography. Write or say your answer clearly.

Close your notes and say aloud: what Guided Writing Grammar Handwriting Punctuation Sentence structure is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Guided Writing Grammar Handwriting Punctuation Sentence structure”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: write common words with correct orthography)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Guided Writing Grammar Handwriting Punctuation Sentence structure to a partner. (skill: appreciate the role of writing in interactive communication contexts)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: write common words with correct orthography)

Example 4: Read a short paragraph about “Guided Writing Grammar Handwriting Punctuation Sentence structure”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: appreciate the role of writing in interactive communication contexts)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Guided Writing Grammar Handwriting Punctuation Sentence structure to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: write common words with correct orthography.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate the role of writing in interactive communication contexts.
4. Practise this skill: write common words with correct orthography.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Guided Writing Grammar Handwriting Punctuation Sentence structure from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Guided Writing Grammar Handwriting Punctuation Sentence structure: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Guided Writing Grammar Handwriting Punctuation Sentence structure?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is proper sequencing of information important while writing?
2. How can you improve your handwriting?
3. Why is correct orthography important?
4. What makes your handwriting unique?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Guided Writing Grammar Handwriting Punctuation Sentence structure means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: write common words with correct orthography.
5. Be able to: appreciate the role of writing in interactive communication contexts.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
